family: small creators talking about a product
text: Find 10 US creators with under 10,000 followers who posted about an AI study or note-taking app in the last 30 days and got a video over 100,000 views.
good: Up to 10 creators, each under 10,000 followers, with a video about an AI study or note-taking app posted in the last 30 days that has over 100,000 views; US marked from the video region with the creator's own country unknown.

family: small creators talking about a product
text: Find sub-10K creators talking about Claude.
good: Creators under 10,000 followers whose videos are about Claude the AI assistant (not people named Claude), each with the video that shows it.

text: Find me 10 NYU creators with around 1,500 followers.
good: Creators whose bio or videos tie them to NYU, with follower counts near 1,500 and the band it used stated; NYU affiliation marked unknown when only a hashtag suggests it.

text: Which small creators are posting toy unboxing videos that blew up this month? I sell blind boxes.
good: Small creators (size band stated as an assumption) with a toy or blind-box unboxing video from this month that far outperformed their usual views.

text: Who is making videos about Pingo AI, the language app? I want creators like them for my Spanish-learning app.
good: Creators with videos about Pingo AI, plus similar language-learning creators, each with proof; sponsorship only from the paid label or bio words.

text: What hooks are working this week for language learning apps?
good: A few hook patterns from this week's language-app videos, each citing at least two videos, described from what is seen or said in the opening seconds.

text: Compare @studyfetch.kendall, @astnstudies and @studywith.karen: who is the best fit to promote a flashcard app?
good: All three creators inspected and compared on reach, consistency and topic fit, with a stated pick and the reason; a missing or inactive account said plainly.

text: Find fitness creators in the UK under 20k followers who post walking or step-challenge content.
good: Creators under 20,000 followers with walking or step-challenge videos from GB-region videos, the creator's own country marked unknown.

family: a poor fit for TikTok creators
text: Find creators who can promote my B2B payroll software to CFOs.
good: Says TikTok is a weak channel for reaching CFOs and states its assumptions; any creators offered are finance or accounting creators with proof, not padding.

text: Find creators who recently partnered with Anthropic.
good: Only creators with a paid label or explicit partnership words on a video about Anthropic or Claude; partnership marked unknown otherwise, and a short answer is acceptable.

text: Why did this video do well? https://www.tiktok.com/@studyfetch.kendall/video/7687877955111947551
good: Watches or reads the video, compares its views with the creator's usual views, and separates what was observed (hook, on-screen text, timing) from the guess at why it worked.
Says the question is underspecified, asks or states what it needs (what the app does, audience, budget), and does not pad with random creators.
